articles.title: Psilocybin-assisted therapy shows promise for veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD
articles.summary: A pilot clinical trial suggests that psilocybin combined with psychotherapy is safe and well-tolerated by veterans with severe, treatment-resistant PTSD. The study found that most participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for PTSD.

articles.title: New space station study reveals a hidden side effect of long-term microgravity on the human brain
articles.summary: Astronauts are notoriously slow and deliberate when moving in space. But a new study from the China Space Station reveals it’s not just about safety—microgravity actually tricks the human brain into underestimating its own body mass.

articles.title: Long COVID symptoms linked to measurable damage in the brain’s dopamine system
articles.summary: A recent study provides evidence that people experiencing long COVID show a measurable reduction in the brain’s dopamine-releasing neurons. These physical changes tend to be associated with persistent symptoms like apathy, memory problems, and slowed physical movements.

articles.title: Cognitive Convergence: Deep Similarities Between Large Language Models and Human Cognition
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are widely regarded as alien intelligences, systems whose cognitive operations are fundamentally unlike our own. articles.title: Three Failures of Pain Location: Why the Diagnostic Utility of Symptom Localization Is Not One Thing
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Patient-reported pain location is diagnostically decisive for some presentations and nearly uninformative for others. The prevailing account treats this as a single gradient of diagnostic utility governed by anatomical complexity. That explanation conflates three epistemically distinct failures of localization, each with its own mathematical structure, optimal instrument, and public-health consequence. articles.title: A behavior-environment information loop drives sensory navigation
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.26295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As organisms navigate the environment to locate critical resources, their behavioral actions must be tightly coupled to their sensory inputs. Here, we introduce an information-theoretic framework that quantifies this coupling using transfer entropy, which measures information flow between sensory inputs and behavioral outputs. articles.title: What if the brain does not create consciousness?
articles.summary: Christof Koch is taking on one of science’s deepest mysteries: how the brain creates conscious experience, or whether it creates it at all. He argues that materialism has yet to solve this “hard problem” and will explore puzzling phenomena such as near-death experiences and terminal lucidity. His work points toward the possibility that consciousness may be woven into reality itself.

articles.title: Childhood emotional abuse predicts lower romantic relationship satisfaction
articles.summary: Adults who experienced psychological maltreatment as children often report lower satisfaction in romantic partnerships. By tracking young adults over time, researchers found that this early abuse diminishes relationship satisfaction by eroding the individual's broader sense of social belonging.

articles.title: Neuroscientists just upended a core assumption about how psychedelics alter brain function
articles.summary: New brain scans show that drugs like LSD, psilocybin, and MDMA reliably reduce the upward flow of information into a core brain network. This surprising shift offers a biological explanation for their psychological risks and benefits.

articles.title: Spicy food can reduce extreme physical pain
articles.summary: A burning mouth might offer temporary relief from physical injuries, according to a recent trial. Researchers discovered that eating spicy food can act as a mild painkiller, dampening the brain's response to intense physical discomfort.

articles.summary: Men who naturally prefer staying up late might face a higher risk of developing premature ejaculation. A new study links this biological sleep preference and symptom severity to daily lifestyle routines and psychological stress.

articles.title: Losing an election is associated with lower social trust among polarized voters
articles.summary: A new study suggests that voters whose preferred party loses a national election experience a decline in generalized social trust. This gap widens among highly polarized voters who harbor strong negative feelings toward opposing political parties.

articles.title: How a child’s brain processes emotional faces offers a surprising glimpse into their future friendships
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a child’s early brain activity can forecast their future social life. Surprisingly, the same neural response to emotional faces predicts very different patterns of peer engagement for boys and girls entering adolescence.
